# Build: per-instance-settings-window-picker

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-13T17:46:43.480Z
> every tab group and toolbar has its own settings interface, and within it you can select our settings interface

## What to build
Continue build "Per-instance settings-window picker inside every tab group and toolbar's settings" (per-instance-settings-window-picker) — Phase 1, model Opus.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-13 17:46):
"every tab group and toolbar has its own settings interface, and within it you can select our settings interface"
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 10 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next. Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Branch: claude/per-instance-settings-window-picker
Steps in this phase (2 left, ~20 min):
[x] s1 (~10 min) Every chrome instance (tab group, toolbar, banner, nav, menu bar) has its own chrome settings dialog (framework ChromeContext.tsx / chrome-settings-rules.mjs). Today the settings asset is picked per type/app (axf.chrome.settings.<type>). Add, inside each instance's settings dialog, a picker to choose which settings interface (settings asset) THAT instance uses, per instance, with the shared default preselected. Changing it re-renders the dialog live. Persist per instance, survive reload, follow skins. Expose via REST/MCP/CLI/voice and control@1. Tests, help entry, Shipped features.
[ ] s2 (~10 min) every tab group and toolbar has its own settings interface, and within it you can select our settings interface
[ ] s3 (~10 min) Tests green, report _claude/builds/reports/per-instance-settings-window-picker.md, THREADS row, commit, push, PR
Read first: _claude/builds/reports/per-instance-settings-window-picker.md, _claude/THREADS.md
Tick each step right after its commit: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step per-instance-settings-window-picker <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). Link your branch / PR: node framework/cli/builds-live.mjs link per-instance-settings-window-picker --branch <b> --pr <n>.
Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

## Pipeline
This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account mossesx-max- for the Opus phase. Work through every step of the phase in this one session: they are checkpoints, not separate tasks. As each step finishes, commit it on your branch, push, and tick it (orchestrator.mjs act step per-instance-settings-window-picker <stepId> done), then go straight on to the next; nothing is lost if the session dies, the next one starts at the first open step on the same branch. When this phase's steps are done, stop: the dispatcher starts the next phase on the right account. If you must stop early with steps left, say why in a build note (orchestrator.mjs act note per-instance-settings-window-picker "…"); the build goes back to Pending for Brett.
